course_name_en: Computer simulation of plastic forming processes
prerequisites: It has a basic understanding of the processes and machinery for plastic forming
It has a basic understanding of the foundations of the theory of finite element methods
It has a basic understanding of the strength of materials, mechanics and the theory of machines and mechanisms

learning_outcomes.text: It knows the construction of mathematical models of plastic forming processes
It has a basic knowledge of the possible applications of the finite element method to the process analysis and optimization of forming processes
It knows the basic relationships between material properties and parameters of forming process
It gain the skills necessary to build mathematical models of plastic forming processes
Is able to perform the calculation and initial optimization of the plastic forming process
Is able to identify which of the process parameters significantly affect the forming forces
It acquires beliefs about the responsibility for the work

syllabus_topics: Plastic forming - types of processes, the basic process parameters
The model of the process, geometry transfer, calculation model building
Models of materials, stress-strain curves, yield criterion
Modelling of bulk metal forming processes - extrusion, drawing
Modelling of bulk metal forming processes - rolling, forging
Introduction to computer simulation of the plastic forming processes in the computing environment
Modelling of selected examples of plastic forming processes
Analysis and determination of the influence of process parameters on the forming forces (friction, temperature, speed)
Preparation of design assumptions for the selected item shaped by forming processes
Description of the process geometry and its export to the FEM program
Building the model in the FEM program
Making calculations for the various process parameters and/or the geometry of the process
teaching_methods: self study - preparation for project class
assessment_rules: The lecture assessment (P) is based on the final test (F1). The project assessment (P) is calculated as the average of the project rating (F1) and a test (F2).

Morawiecki M., Sadok L., Wosiek E.: Przeróbka plastyczna- podstawy teoretyczne. Wydawnictwo Śląsk 1986
Gabryszewski Z., Gronostajski J.: Mechanika procesów obróbki plastycznej, PWN, Warszawa 1991
degree: Mechanical Engineering and Machine Building (I level, full-time)
